title: kbjob.py serve runs the queued jobs of its host one after another, each as a process group of its own with its output kept
goal: python3 _tools/kbjob.py [--store PATH] serve [--once] runs the queued jobs of its own host, clone and operator in submit order, one at a time: it takes a job with the lease jobrun/JB-... (ttl 60 s, renewed every 20 s while the child runs), moves it queued to running, runs the operation's argv from kj_ops.OPS in the clone as the leader of a process group of its own with stdin closed and stdout and stderr appended to kb-jobs/JB-.../output.log under the clone's git common directory, and moves it to succeeded (exit 0), refused (exit 1 and a line land stopped at step NAME: or another stop line naming a step: that step, as bl_land.land_refused_step reads it) or failed (any other end, with the exit and the last output line), each move through the job table of ST-hojylkmb; kj_exec.classify(exit, text) is that rule as a pure function; --once drains the queue and exits 0 (1 when a job failed); a job of another operator or host stays queued; a second serve on one host exits 0 naming the running one's pid (an exclusive file in the host lock directory holding pid, clone and start time, cleared when the pid is gone, as kg_lock does)

run: import sys,os,tempfile,json,subprocess; sys.path.insert(0,"_tools"); import kj_store; s=os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(),"c.sqlite"); a=kj_store.submit(".","check","","claude-0123abcd",{"name":"backlog-check"},store=s); r=subprocess.run([sys.executable,"_tools/kbjob.py","--store",s,"serve","--once"],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=300); st=kj_store.status(".",a["job"],store=s); assert r.returncode in (0,1) and st["state"] in ("succeeded","failed") and st["log"] and os.path.exists(st["log"]) and "errors=" in open(st["log"]).read(), (r, st); assert [e["fields"]["state"] for e in st["events"]][:2]==["queued","running"]

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,"_tools"); import kj_exec; c=kj_exec.classify; assert c(0,"")==("succeeded",None); assert c(1,"land stopped at step rebase: conflict")==("refused","rebase"); assert c(1,"boom")==("failed",None); assert c(2,"usage")==("failed",None)

import sys,os,tempfile,subprocess,time; d=tempfile.mkdtemp(); env=dict(os.environ,KB_HOST_LOCK_DIR=d); s=os.path.join(d,"c.sqlite"); cmd=[sys.executable,"_tools/kbjob.py","--store",s,"serve"]; p=subprocess.Popen(cmd,env=env,stdout=subprocess.PIPE,text=True); time.sleep(3); r=subprocess.run(cmd,env=env,capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=30); p.terminate(); assert r.returncode==0 and str(p.pid) in (r.stdout+r.stderr), (r, p.pid)

import sys,os,tempfile,json,subprocess; sys.path.insert(0,"_tools"); import kj_store
s=os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(),"c.sqlite"); co=lambda *x: subprocess.run([sys.executable,"_tools/coord.py","--store",s,*x],capture_output=True,text=True)
a=kj_store.submit(".","check","","claude-0123abcd",{"name":"backlog-check"},store=s); g=json.loads(co("get","job/"+a["job"]).stdout); rec=json.loads(g["value"]); rec["operator"]="op-00000000"
assert co("put","job/"+a["job"],"--value",json.dumps(rec),"--revision",str(g["revision"])).returncode==0
subprocess.run([sys.executable,"_tools/kbjob.py","--store",s,"serve","--once"],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=300)
assert kj_store.status(".",a["job"],store=s)["state"]=="queued"

gates.question: How does kj_exec read a stop line that names a step, and which exit does a record keep for a signalled child?
options: own pattern in kj_exec: any line 'NAME stopped at step STEP:' on exit 1, the step as an ops token; a signal 128 plus the number
import bl_land.land_refused_step: land stop lines only; a signal kept as the negative code
gates.recommendation: own pattern in kj_exec: any line 'NAME stopped at step STEP:' on exit 1, the step as an ops token; a signal 128 plus the number
gates.reason: so classify stays pure and light and a job field holds digits only
gates.answer: own pattern in kj_exec: any line 'NAME stopped at step STEP:' on exit 1, the step as an ops token; a signal 128 plus the number

gates.question: What does serve do when it is not told --once and the queue is empty, and what happens to a running job when serve gets a signal?
options: poll every 5 s (KB_JOB_POLL) and run until a signal; a signal ends the child's group and moves the job to lost
exit when the queue is empty; a signal leaves the job running

gates.reason: the one state the job table gives a job whose runner is gone

gates.question: Which name does the host lock file of serve take, and where does serve print a failed job's last output line?
options: kb-jobs-serve.lock in the host lock directory; the last line goes to serve's own output, the log keeps all
a name per clone; the last line goes into the job record
gates.recommendation: kb-jobs-serve.lock in the host lock directory; the last line goes to serve's own output, the log keeps all
gates.reason: because a job event takes no free text

notes: Choices: the executor is a plain loop in the clone's own python, not a new daemon framework; it reads the same store as every session (coord.project_store, coord.py:1561), so a clone's sessions and its executor meet in one file with no network (coordination.md:8). The child is started as dispatch starts a detached worker (bl_dispatch.py:1051 spawn_detached: start_new_session, stdin DEVNULL, log file) and killed as kg_lock.end_group does (TERM, then KILL of the group). One job at a time here; ordering across classes and the parallel slots are ST-serialisation. Exit rule reuses bl_land.land_refused_step (bl_land.py:2372). An output log is kept per job under kb-jobs/ in the git common directory (outside the tree, never committed). Evidence: backlog.py landings over the query log, 2026-11-08: kbgit.py sync --push step median 29.8 s p95 176 s (n=2977, real items); checks step p95 38 s; so a single job runs from seconds to minutes. No test added (ceiling). Order agreed 2026-11-08 with SP-ep7ck2ab's manager (ask A1e21b0d155): shared kb/_self/map.csv rows land by first claim, the later item rebases; no hard dependency.
